events.what: 321-point three-distance configuration in R^63 proving b(63) >= 65, lowering the smallest known counterexample dimension from 64 to 63; produced by Grinsztajn prompting GPT-5.5 Pro
events.ai_basis: Record: Wikipedia's AI-discoveries list credits Max Grinsztajn, prompting GPT-5.5 Pro, in May 2026, as the original discoverer; the independent Ji reproduction states 'The example and proof were generated entirely by ChatGPT'.

events.what: Ji's arXiv writeup of the same dimension-63 configuration (GPT 5.6 Sol), withdrawn two days later once priority was clarified
events.ai_basis: The example and proof were generated entirely by ChatGPT using GPT 5.6 Sol.

events.what: Tolmachev and Voronov lower the upper bound on the Borsuk number in R^4 from 9 to 8 by a human-constructed partition

judgement.doubts: Agree with the current codes. The bullet asks for bounds on b(n); the conjecture was already refuted in 1993, so the dimension-63 object moves the smallest known failing dimension (F3), a bound. The R^4 upper bound 9 -> 8 is a second, human bound at the same tier; per step 4 the AI role is the stronger, generated. Ji's withdrawal was for priority, not a mathematical error, so it is not a knock-down; it is a duplicate of the Grinsztajn event. The Grinsztajn May 2026 date and GPT-5.5 Pro attribution rest on secondary compilations (Lean PR, Wikipedia list); if they fail, Ji's (also AI-generated) writeup still supports the same codes. Verification counted as checkable: an explicit finite configuration verified by exact computation, not just a Lean build.
